text: Every release goes out as a canary. The new version first gets only twenty percent of the traffic.

text: I hear SLO, SLI and error budget all the time. What do they actually mean?

text: An SLI, a service level indicator, is simply something we measure. Here there are two: the share of requests that fail with a server error, and how long requests take. For time we use the p95: ninety-five percent of requests are faster than this value.
tts: An S-L-I, a service level indicator, is simply something we measure. Here there are two: the share of requests that fail with a server error, and how long requests take. For time we use the P ninety-five: ninety-five percent of requests are faster than this value.

text: The SLO, the service level objective, is the target for that measurement. For this orders API: 99.5% of requests must succeed, and the p95 must stay under 300 ms.
tts: The S-L-O, the service level objective, is the target for that measurement. For this orders A-P-I: ninety-nine point five percent of requests must succeed, and the P ninety-five must stay under 300 milliseconds.

text: The error budget is what is left over. If 99.5% must succeed, then 0.5% may fail. That is not a failure of the team: it is a budget the team is allowed to spend, on releases, experiments and bad luck.
tts: The error budget is what is left over. If ninety-nine point five percent must succeed, then zero point five percent may fail. That is not a failure of the team: it is a budget the team is allowed to spend, on releases, experiments and bad luck.

text: And the burn rate says how fast you are spending it. A burn rate of one spends the budget exactly over thirty days. A burn rate of 14.4 spends two percent of the whole month's budget in a single hour. That is fast enough to wake someone up.
tts: And the burn rate says how fast you are spending it. A burn rate of one spends the budget exactly over thirty days. A burn rate of fourteen point four spends two percent of the whole month's budget in a single hour. That is fast enough to wake someone up.

text: So how does the canary check turn the SLO into a yes or no?
